local_checks.invariant: Dependency and build resolution must not promote a lower-trust namespace or mutable input into privileged output.
local_checks.result: The only declared build backend is setuptools.build_meta with setuptools>=68; runtime requirements are PyYAML>=6.0,<7 and sqlglot>=27.0,<28. No direct URLs, private namespaces, fallback indexes or custom hooks are declared. Tracked-file inventory has no lockfile, requirements override, pip configuration, submodules or alternate build scripts. Ranges alone do not establish an unauthorized actor or boundary crossing. Historical validation version statements are not current resolved dependency evidence; no CVE status is asserted.

local_checks.invariant: Only intended release inputs should enter artifacts, and untrusted CI events must not inherit publication authority.
local_checks.result: Setuptools package discovery is scoped to src; readme is explicit. Tracked inventory contains no CI workflows, Dockerfile, runnable Compose definition, release/signing/update automation or custom publisher. No source-visible protected token or privileged event is present to trace. Ignore rules exclude virtual environments, build/dist, egg metadata, .spandiff, work and environment files except .env.example. Actual built artifact contents were not executed or inspected and no sensitive inclusion is established.

local_checks.invariant: Obvious hardcoded credentials, checked-in credential files and working seed credentials must not supply an unauthorized principal.
local_checks.result: Tracked path inventory contains no .env, credential JSON, PEM or key file. Broad secret-related scans returned paths only, avoiding credential contents; stricter assignment/key-format path-only scans found no matches. Example credentials are environment-variable references; model requires uppercase identifier references. Doctor reports presence, and adapter forwards only configured referenced values. No credential file or ambient environment was read. No source-grounded real credential disclosure or production-working seed credential was established.

local_checks.invariant: Debug gates and administrative/status/config endpoints must not expose a privileged running service.
local_checks.result: The shipped entrypoint is a local argparse CLI with version/import/doctor commands. Source-wide endpoint/debug searches found no server framework, route registration, listener or debug environment gate. The example fixture returns deterministic in-memory values without starting a server. Thus /debug, /admin, /test, /status, /health, /metrics, /env, /.env and /config endpoint exposure has no implemented server sink. The example health_path is configuration for an external trusted repository.

local_checks.invariant: Dynamic code and security bypass comments must not provide an overlooked execution path.
local_checks.result: Source/example searches found no eval, exec, dynamic __import__, importlib loader, Function or vm execution. Package version uses standard importlib.metadata. YAML uses a SafeLoader subclass. Commands use argv subprocess calls or injected trusted runners, with deeper subprocess boundaries assigned to hunt_execution. Path-only security TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX scan across source/tests/examples/docs found no matching comments.

local_checks.invariant: CORS, cookies, redirects, TLS and error handling must not expose an overlooked remote browser/service boundary.
local_checks.result: No HTTP response server, CORS header configuration or cookie/session writer is implemented, so wildcard credentialed CORS and cookie flags have no source sink. Requests are delegated to an integrator callback. Standalone destination policy permits explicitly approved HTTP or HTTPS and restricts redirects to the same normalized host; deployment TLS is not established by the repository. Local CLI diagnostics can include user-selected paths and parser errors but do not serve production HTTP stack traces or SQL errors. Redirect/transport integration is assigned to hunt_network.

hardening: For repeatable controlled releases, maintain an reviewed dependency lock or constraints file with artifact hashes and bounded build-tool versions; current mutable ranges do not alone demonstrate a vulnerability.
When CI/release automation is introduced, explicitly bind tested artifact identity to publication and narrow job permissions; no such workflow currently exists in tracked source.

local_checks.invariant: Lower-trust trace and result prose must not acquire executable authority in the evidence interpretation workflow.
local_checks.result: The skill limits use to inspecting/explaining results, explicitly denies authority to run trace commands, mutate repositories, read credentials or publish, and treats imperative trace/report content as untrusted. These written instructions are not deterministic isolation. Source inspection finds no model client, prompt assembly, dispatcher, tool handler, persistent model memory, or agent-executed action consumer to establish a code-level authority crossing. ResultV1 retains arbitrary JSON data, but arbitrary permitted prose alone does not establish a vulnerable sink. Evaluations assert fixture structure and text only, not model compliance.

hardening: Keep sanitization scope explicit: imported non-attribute metadata and arbitrary ResultV1/lifecycle caller dictionaries are not automatically credential-redacted. Add explicit source-to-export contracts before integrating persistence or publication; current source does not establish an unauthorized reader.

sanitize_url retains URL authority (including userinfo) and path by design and has no source-visible production caller. Consider rejecting/removing userinfo before introducing a diagnostic/export consumer.
Evaluation tests validate case metadata and safety wording rather than exercising an interpreting model; retain this distinction when reporting verification.

local_checks.result: compose.py:69-75 stop only checks runner presence, invokes command('down','--volumes') with resolved repository cwd and an empty environment, and checks returncode. It neither calls validate nor requires successful start nor consults ownership registration. Constructor only requires an existing repository path; therefore direct stop and stop after validate/credential/up failures are source-reachable for a privileged library caller. command uses the same configured -f and derived -p as startup; app_service does not narrow down. config_from_mapping rejects POSIX absolute/parent traversal but stop has no resolved containment check, including for symlink or directly constructed RepositoryConfig. These are bypasses of startup checks, but config/repository authors and runner-providing integrators are trusted in this product, and no lower-trust selector caller is established. Existing adapter tests cover start/validate/readiness, not stop; they were read, not executed.

local_checks.invariant: A name/label collision becomes a security issue only if a less-trusted selector obtains destructive authority over another principal's resources.
local_checks.result: compose.py:25,34-38 lowercases and replaces non [a-z0-9-] runs with '-', strips edge hyphens, and concatenates project and experiment with '-'. Accepted project values a.b and a_b normalize equally; project/experiment pairs ('a-b','c') and ('a','b-c') concatenate equally; experiment_id has no format validation. project_name alone reaches -p; network_name and volume_name are descriptive values with no Docker label inspection or token binding. Thus namespace uniqueness is not guaranteed and stop can emit identical destructive argv across distinct logical inputs. README safety scope limits execution to trusted repositories/synthetic data. There is no source-visible lower-trust selector principal, maintained effective Docker deployment, pinned Compose policy, or shared victim Docker resource. A namespace collision is therefore a concrete hardening concern rather than an established authorization failure; no unobserved Docker deletion effect is claimed.

local_checks.invariant: Do not assume registered cleanup ownership protects Compose teardown unless an actual source connection attaches those controls.
local_checks.result: Repository-wide symbol/call search found ComposeAdapter references only in its definition, adapter exports, and adapter tests; no tracked call to stop and no Compose cleanup handler/runner implementation exists. CleanupManager._resources filters registrations by experiment, rejects unknown/duplicate IDs, then passes OwnedResource including ownership_token to injected handlers. LifecycleJournal.register_resource stores caller-provided nonempty fields. tests/test_cleanup.py uses recording/failing lambdas rather than ComposeAdapter, and coordinator accepts a generic callback. CLI offers version/import/doctor only. Hence cleanup registration does not bind Compose stop, but neither does a registered-resource attack path reach stop in source. No token-check bypass or active cancellation-to-Docker chain is established. Source-only coverage settles the current boundary; no deployment fact is required to reject an unsupported finding.

critic_reason: The selected namespace companion currently shares one start-oriented check. Source has a distinct destructive lifecycle mode: stop constructs docker compose down --volumes without calling validate, does not require a successful start, and uses only the lossy derived namespace/config path rather than a registered ownership token. Trace stop-only and failed-start teardown, namespace equivalence and any actual cleanup integration. This requests source coverage, not a finding: no remote deployment or unauthorized selector principal is assumed. local_checks.invariant: Collector finalization and retry must not create persistent work or cross a lower-trust authority boundary.
local_checks.result: accept stores counters only and quarantines calls after finalization. flush polls an injected trusted callback until its clock deadline; no repository source consumer connects CollectorSession to shared-service resources, cleanup, verdict, or CLI execution. Finalized replay incorrectly erases a previous timeout, and callback duration is not preempted, but current impact is caller-local state/robustness, without a demonstrated lower-trust shared resource effect. No target code executed.

hardening: src/spandiff/collection/flush.py:35-46: retain the first FlushResult and preserve failed flushed/complete state on repeated flush; finalized currently returns flushed=True and potentially complete=True after a timeout. Add a timeout-then-repeat regression. No implemented security consumer was found.

src/spandiff/collection/flush.py:38-43: validate finite nonnegative timeout and define callback deadline/cancellation contract. Polling is a busy loop and cannot preempt a blocking trusted callback. No shared or cross-principal availability effect is established by repository source.

src/spandiff/orchestration/coordinator.py:53-54: bind returned variant, revision and batch_id as well as fixture_id to the requested run before marking comparable. Callback is supplied by trusted integrator; mismatch is evidence-integrity robustness without an implemented privilege boundary.

src/spandiff/reporting/result.py:44-66: validate result_state and cleanup_state types/enums, completeness consistency and finite JSON numbers. Deserialization currently checks container shape rather than evidence authenticity or semantic consistency; no source authentication or authoritative approval claim exists.

src/spandiff/normalization/grouping.py:28-45: use a tuple for parent_path components and stable semantic-derived group identifiers when comparing separately grouped sets. Slash joins can collide, adding an earlier sorted operation shifts ordinal group IDs, and semantic ambiguity check cannot observe distinct shapes already separated by the key. No source automatic join into comparison or security action was found.

src/spandiff/collection/coverage.py:19-35 and src/spandiff/comparison/structural.py:28-39: validate public library numeric types and finite/range constraints consistently; add zero/negative/boolean/nonfinite boundary cases. Structural changed-count and changed-error checks are mutually exclusive, so simultaneous changes emit only the count rule. These are misleading evidence/robustness issues, not established lower-trust authority effects.

src/spandiff/comparison/timing.py:99-101: batch_counts scans selected samples once per unique batch, producing quadratic caller-local work when each sample has a unique batch. No service entry point/shared blast radius is implemented, so this is optimization hardening.

None of these is a universal secret classifier. The implemented import CLI exports only counts and operator-selected file paths, not imported attributes or names. SQL/HTTP identities have no implemented automatic connection to report export. Lifecycle transition accepts caller detail JSON without sanitizing, but no production caller or credential-to-detail/unauthorized-reader path is present. Database module defines schema/migration only; no trace persistence writer joins these stages. Report renderers serialize supplied result data to the same local operator; no sharing or distinct-reader policy is implemented. No concrete data-boundary failure survives source tracing.

local_checks.invariant: Configuration parsing must not execute YAML constructors, resolve credential values, run commands or promote parsed data into filesystem authority.
local_checks.result: _UniqueSafeLoader subclasses yaml.SafeLoader and installs a mapping constructor that rejects duplicate keys. Strict mapping, field, scalar, command-array and credential-reference validation follows parsing. Parsing performs no command execution or environment resolution. The connected doctor path checks file presence and environment-reference presence without spawning configured commands or returning credential values. Arbitrary operator-selected configuration paths are intentional, and repository authors are trusted to select execution configuration. YAML depth/alias limits and malformed unhashable-key exception normalization are robustness concerns in this local parsing context, not demonstrated security-boundary failures. Existing tests were inspected only.

hardening: Replace CLI full read_text with a bounded binary read before decoding, rejecting max_bytes + 1 bytes; independently reconsidered prior fingerprint spandiff/import/prelimit-full-read is hardening because the implemented interface affects the selecting local operator's process and establishes no shared-service boundary.
Consider total-span and issue-count caps, JSON/YAML nesting limits, and bounded scalar conversion to improve resilience against malformed local evidence and configuration.
Normalize malformed container and YAML mapping-key failures into ImportValidationError or ConfigurationError so local invalid input produces consistent diagnostics.

local_checks.invariant: SQL normalization cost and failures must have a source-grounded input path and meaningful shared-resource consequence before being classified as an availability vulnerability.
local_checks.result: sql.py:20 rejects nonstrings and blank strings. Lines 23-27 invoke SQLGlot parsing, literal transformation and SQL generation without a local byte, tree-depth or node budget. Only ParseError and UnsupportedError from parse_one are converted to unknown; transformation and generation are outside the try. pyproject.toml:11 permits SQLGlot 27.x and does not establish a particular installed implementation. Source establishes no parser growth curve, recursion failure input or SQLGlot vulnerability; none is claimed. No target code or dependency was executed.

local_checks.invariant: Parallel HTTP normalization and grouping must be checked for effective bounds, failure propagation, retained resources and amplification.
local_checks.result: http.py:26-29 rejects disallowed services and invalid methods, but target has no explicit type/length guard and urlsplit at line 30 has no exception conversion. The segment patterns use fixed-width UUID syntax or simple character-class repetition; no catastrophic-backtracking construction is source-visible. Path splitting retains per-input segment copies and drops query/fragment values. grouping.py:34 bounds parent ancestry to eight entries, but not entry lengths; lines 39-46 consume all observations, retain every member and sort distinct keys. The functions have no global cache, queue, worker, subprocess, network fetch, persistent state or retry loop; objects are returned to the caller and no separate cleanup owner exists. Total work/cardinality is caller supplied, with no established cross-principal retention or shared pool impact.

local_checks.invariant: Normalization exceptions and cost may be promoted to a security candidate only when an implemented caller connects lower-trust input to a shared service, another principal or operator-owned spend.
local_checks.result: Source-wide reference search found normalize_sql, normalize_http and group_operations only at definitions and normalization package exports, with no application call sites. CLI import reads two local files and calls import_otlp_json; it emits only counts/provenance and never normalizes SQL/HTTP or groups observations. The importer advertises max_bytes=50000000 and max_spans=100000, but these are not asserted as bounds on direct library normalization calls because no connection exists. CompareCoordinator invokes an integrator-supplied callback and catches Exception into a failed VariantRun; no source wiring invokes normalization through it. compare_groups accepts already supplied summaries and does not invoke normalizers. Thus a malformed or expensive library input can at most be shown here to affect its invoking local process; no implemented supervisor/shared-service blast radius, paid amplification or cross-principal availability consequence is established. Missing limits and exception consistency remain hardening, not speculative needs_validation findings.

critic_reason: The selected parser-cost companion is checked only on the OTLP JSON import path. SQL normalization is a separate lower-trust observation parser: parse_one, recursive tree transformation and SQL regeneration have no local input-size/depth budget, and only two parser exception classes are normalized. Existing normalization review checks leakage, while wildcard checks do not include SQL/HTTP normalization paths. Review cost/error propagation and actual callers, with HTTP parsing as the parallel path; do not infer an integration, superlinear algorithm or cross-principal availability consequence absent from source.
hardening: Before connecting normalization to automated trace ingestion, add explicit SQL/HTTP input-size and SQL tree-complexity limits, and a grouping observation/cardinality budget. The last-eight-parent rule bounds ancestry count only. Current source has no shared-resource caller, so the absent budgets alone are not an availability finding.

Define a consistent metadata-only failure contract across SQL parsing/transformation/generation and HTTP URL parsing; include bounded malformed-input regression cases when execution is authorized. Current exception gaps do not establish a fatal shared-process security boundary, and no SQLGlot CVE or superlinear complexity is asserted.

local_checks.result: Registration persists experiment-qualified resource rows and nonempty ownership fields. Cleanup enumerates using experiment_id, rejects unknown/duplicate selectors before handler calls, passes the registered ownership token and locator, qualifies updates by experiment/resource, skips cleaned rows and records missing/failed handlers as pending. Cancellation marks results incomplete. Handlers are injected trusted callbacks; no implemented queue, restore reader or deletion/retention guarantee establishes a later unauthorized data consumer. Existing tests describe retry/idempotence and unknown-resource rejection but were not executed. Aggregate cleanup state after subset cleanup and registration after cleanup are operational hardening opportunities without an established security impact.

Compute experiment cleanup_state from all registered resource rows after subset cleanup, rather than only the selected batch; define whether resource registration is allowed after cleanup.

Coverage rejects absent denominators, undercorrelation, and nonzero orphan/missing/dropped counts. Verdict validates booleans and nonnegative integer count/budget values and prioritizes incompleteness. CLI import explicitly emits incomplete state and exit 2; it does not join coverage/comparison/verdict. Grouping, summary, and ResultV1 validation have robustness gaps recorded as hardening, but source callers establish no authorization, cleanup, deployment approval, resource ownership, or shared execution consequence. hardening: src/spandiff/collection/flush.py:35-46: retain the first FlushResult and preserve failed flushed/complete state on repeated flush; finalized currently returns flushed=True and potentially complete=True after a timeout. Add a timeout-then-repeat regression. No implemented security consumer was found.

src/spandiff/collection/flush.py:38-43: validate finite nonnegative timeout and define callback deadline/cancellation contract. Polling is a busy loop and cannot preempt a blocking trusted callback. No shared or cross-principal availability effect is established by repository source.

src/spandiff/orchestration/coordinator.py:53-54: bind returned variant, revision and batch_id as well as fixture_id to the requested run before marking comparable. Callback is supplied by trusted integrator; mismatch is evidence-integrity robustness without an implemented privilege boundary.

src/spandiff/reporting/result.py:44-66: validate result_state and cleanup_state types/enums, completeness consistency and finite JSON numbers. Deserialization currently checks container shape rather than evidence authenticity or semantic consistency; no source authentication or authoritative approval claim exists.

src/spandiff/normalization/grouping.py:28-45: use a tuple for parent_path components and stable semantic-derived group identifiers when comparing separately grouped sets. Slash joins can collide, adding an earlier sorted operation shifts ordinal group IDs, and semantic ambiguity check cannot observe distinct shapes already separated by the key. No source automatic join into comparison or security action was found.

src/spandiff/collection/coverage.py:19-35 and src/spandiff/comparison/structural.py:28-39: validate public library numeric types and finite/range constraints consistently; add zero/negative/boolean/nonfinite boundary cases. Structural changed-count and changed-error checks are mutually exclusive, so simultaneous changes emit only the count rule. These are misleading evidence/robustness issues, not established lower-trust authority effects.

src/spandiff/comparison/timing.py:99-101: batch_counts scans selected samples once per unique batch, producing quadratic caller-local work when each sample has a unique batch. No service entry point/shared blast radius is implemented, so this is optimization hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Follow repository-selected Git work through the actual default subprocess runners and buffered output; establish a lower-trust input and meaningful resource impact beyond intended local operator work before reporting exhaustion.
local_checks.result: revisions.py:37 runs rev-parse/worktree add/remove synchronously with capture_output=True, text=True and no timeout; commit stdout is checked only after completion. snapshot.py:36 similarly captures all stdout/stderr without a timeout. capture:46-64 obtains the full binary tracked diff before hashing, retains it while listing all untracked names, then decodes/splits and creates tuples/sets/lists before exclusions. Costs can scale with operator-selected repository contents, tracked modifications, untracked cardinality, Git behavior and inherited configuration. No byte/cardinality/time bound is present. README safety explicitly scopes execution to trusted repositories; classes have no application callers beyond exports and tests, and CLI dispatch exposes no revision/snapshot operation. No remote caller, distinct lower-trust repository principal, shared worker pool, external paid resource, or other-principal availability effect is established. These are concrete local resource hardening gaps, not a surviving security candidate. Tests use FakeGit and do not exercise actual process/output limits; none were executed.

local_checks.invariant: Check cancellation ownership, process lifetime and temporary resource recovery on the concrete default Git paths without attributing injected fixture callback behavior to them.
local_checks.result: Both concrete defaults call subprocess.run synchronously and retain no PID/process-group handle or cancellation/deadline parameter. Revision create/remove operates on validated owned-root variant paths, but a failed worktree add has no explicit rollback, and no Git subprocess registration or wiring to CleanupManager is implemented. CleanupManager.cancel only transitions the journal; it does not interrupt either Git runner, while cleanup invokes externally supplied handlers. Source therefore does not establish cancellation propagation or descendant-process containment, but also does not establish an abandoned shared process, repeating handle leak, retained cross-principal resource, or cancellation-return path that leaves Git work running. OS-specific subprocess interruption/descendant behavior was not assumed or executed. Under the local trusted operator model these remain hardening observations rather than findings.

critic_reason: Current Git units cover shell/ownership and snapshot filename/output selection; their exact maps exclude the resource companion. Fixture cancellation coverage concludes no default subprocess runner exists on its fixture boundary. In contrast both Git helpers implement subprocess.run(capture_output=True) without timeout, and snapshot capture fully buffers binary git diff and untracked filename output before hashing/filtering. These concrete same-path alternate sinks merit explicit buffering, cancellation and process-lifetime coverage even if the trusted-repository/local-operator contract ultimately makes all observations hardening.
hardening: Bound stdout/stderr in both default Git runners and hash tracked diff incrementally; cap untracked-name bytes/count before decoding and materializing tuples, sets and sorted lists. Current memory growth consumes the selecting operator process and has no source-established shared-service blast radius.

Add explicit Git operation deadlines and cancellation ownership if orchestration is connected to execution: process-group lifecycle, wait/reap, and exact owned-worktree cleanup after failed or interrupted creation. Current journal cancellation is not wired to either default Git runner, and no concrete retained descendant or shared-pool leak was established.

Existing Git unit tests use injected FakeGit responses; future bounded isolated default-runner tests should check output ceilings, cancellation and failure cleanup. No target processes or tests were run during this source-only review.

local_checks.invariant: Destination policy must reject unapproved HTTP hosts and cross-host redirects before returning an approved destination.
local_checks.result: from_hosts lowercases and removes trailing dots and rejects an empty effective allowlist. validate uses urlsplit hostname, requires http/https, and checks exact membership before calling an optional resolver. Supplied private/loopback or malformed resolver addresses fail. Output reconstructs scheme, normalized host, and path, removing query, fragment, credentials and explicit port. validate_redirect checks normalized original/target hostname equality and then re-applies the target allowlist/address check. Relative redirects are rejected. Optional resolver omission or empty results skip address protection, and policy has no DNS-to-connection binding, but this standalone helper makes no fetch. Existing tests assert query removal, disallowed host/private answers, and alternate-host redirect rejection; tests were not run.

local_checks.invariant: A potential SSRF path must connect lower-trust URL selection to a repository-implemented network operation across an authority boundary.
local_checks.result: Source references to DestinationPolicy are its export and standalone tests; ScenarioRunner accepts an injected requester and passes a scenario method/path/headers/timeout, with no implemented URL join, DNS resolution, HTTP client, redirect follower, or connection sink. Parsed scenario and health paths require a leading slash and reject queries; network-path references beginning // are not excluded, but any authority reinterpretation depends on an absent callback implementation. Compose readiness also receives only an injected check. No source-visible path takes lower-trust URLs through this helper into privileged transport. Consequently optional resolver and future parser/transport mismatch concerns are hardening rather than an SSRF candidate or an invented deployment blocker.

hardening: Before exposing execution to less-trusted configuration, wire ExecutionLimits into ScenarioRunner, cap the combined warmup/measured count, clamp request deadlines, and define aggregate experiment accounting; max_concurrency is currently unused because the runner is sequential. The previous spandiff/limits/scenario-consumer-gap lead does not meet the availability candidate gate in this local operator/callback-only implementation.

Before adding a concrete HTTP transport, require complete DNS checks when reject_private is true (including IP literals and empty resolver answers), bind validated addresses to connections and validate redirects through the same transport policy. Preserve or explicitly reject ports and IPv6 authorities rather than reconstructing ambiguous URLs; reject network-path scenario references if URL joining will be used. These are future integration safeguards; no implemented fetch crosses this boundary today.
